extracted.intended_audience: teachers, school administrators, educational philosophers, and students of education
extracted.subtask_description: Principles and criteria for moral education and the relation of knowledge to conduct in democratic schooling, drawn from an educational-philosophical chapter discussing methods of knowing, social conditions, and curricular/organizational requirements for moral training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critique of the scholastic/formal-discipline method
rubrics_metrics.description: The scholastic method (formal logic, doctrine of formal discipline) treats thought as a formal activity applied to any material and often means 'making distinctions, definitions, divisions, and classifications for the mere sake of making them' with no objective in experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid instruction that emphasizes abstract formal operations detached from concrete subject-matter and practical ends. Anti-patterns include systematizing or exercising mental forms as ends in themselves rather than as tools for understanding lived experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of particulars and generals (avoid sensationalism/rationalism split)
rubrics_metrics.description: Real knowledge requires both particularizing (specifying facts via sense experience) and generalizing (bringing prior experience to bear to perceive significance). Sensationalism (bare facts) and rationalism (bare relations) are one-sided if isolated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design learning so that particulars (direct observations, fragmentary data) are explicitly connected to general meanings and prior experience; exercises should require students to specify facts and then recombine them to discover connections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pragmatic continuity of knowing with purposive activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowledge should be continuous with an activity which purposely modifies the environment; the essential feature of the pragmatic method is maintaining this continuity of knowing with doing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor curricular tasks that require purposeful modification of the environment (projects, occupations, problem-solving) so knowledge is learned as an instrument of action, not as inert information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge as organized dispositions and habits enabling adaptation
rubrics_metrics.description: Only that which has been organized into our disposition so as to enable us to adapt the environment to our needs and to adapt our aims and desires to the situation in which we live is really knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess knowledge by observable dispositions and capacities to act intelligently in situations (habits, problem-solving tendencies), not merely by verbal recall. Emphasize practice and habituation that integrate ideas into conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connect school learning with activities/occupations in a medium of associated life
rubrics_metrics.description: The educational equivalent of pragmatic knowledge is the connection of the acquisition of knowledge in the schools with activities or occupations carried on in a medium of associated life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure learning around cooperative, occupational, or project-based activities that resemble real social roles; use workshops, labs, shops, and cooperative tasks to situate learning in social practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid sharp dualism of inner (motive) vs outer (conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Moral theories that split motive/character (inner) from conduct/consequences (outer) are misleading; conscious motives are part of continuous activity and not a realm wholly separate from action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral education should not treat 'meaning well' or private motives as sufficient; nor should it reduce morality to mere outward conformity. Design experiences that integrate inner deliberation and outward consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conscious deliberation as formative phase of action (mental/psychical phase)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliberation and desire represent nascent activities—an indeterminate, formative phase that issues later in overt acts; conscious reflection reorganizes dispositions when routine habits are blocked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create learning situations that legitimately produce hesitation and require reflection (problems, dilemmas) so students practice coordinating internal deliberation with later action; avoid substituting fantasy for practical testing of ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discipline imagination with reference to practicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Imagination can run loose when not checked by conditions of practicability, leading to 'building castles in the air' rather than using imaginative constructions to find practical solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete constraints and opportunities for testing imaginative solutions; favor imaginative proposals that are linked to feasible planning and execution rather than purely escapist fantasies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide progressive cumulative undertakings engaging interest and requiring reflection
rubrics_metrics.description: Moral dispositions arise when individuals engage in a consecutively developing undertaking which engages their interest and requires reflection—only then do desire and thought become organic factors in overt conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design curricula as progressive, cumulative projects wherein students' sustained interest and reflection are necessary to succeed; anti-patterns include disconnected exercises and rote tasks that don't demand continuity of purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favor interest-in-occupation over abstract duty for persistence
rubrics_metrics.description: Interest in the occupation as a whole (its continuous development) keeps a pupil at work through distractions and difficulties more effectively than appeals to abstract duty; self and interest are continuous—interest reveals the kind of self being formed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate genuine vocational or project interest so students persist; avoid relying primarily on exhortations to duty or abstract principles without embedding them in meaningful activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge must be first-hand/practical to shape character
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowledge gained at first hand through the exigencies of experience affects conduct; second-hand, devitalized information (book-learning aimed at recitation) has little influence on character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize experiential, practice-based learning; evaluate knowledge by its integration into routines and choices rather than mere ability to recite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual traits are moral qualities
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualities of mind—open-mindedness, single-mindedness, sincerity, breadth of outlook, thoroughness, assumption of responsibility—are intrinsically moral traits and central to moral education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat intellectual habits as targets of moral education; include criteria for assessing these dispositions (e.g., willingness to revise views, thoroughness, responsibility for consequences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral and social dimensions of conduct are identical
rubrics_metrics.description: Morals are as broad as acts concerning our relationships with others; virtues are not isolated traits but are central because they carry with them thousands of other attitudes—virtue concerns the whole character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame moral education in terms of social relationships and whole-character development rather than lists of isolated virtues; design assessments and experiences that reflect integrated social functioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: School must function as a genuine community life
rubrics_metrics.description: Social perceptions and interests develop only in a genuine social medium—'the school must itself be a community life' with give-and-take in building a common experience; playgrounds, shops, workrooms, laboratories promote intercourse and cooperation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize schools to enable real cooperation and shared problem-solving across curricular and extracurricular settings; evaluate school organization by the degree to which it creates authentic shared experiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning in school should be continuous with life outside school
rubrics_metrics.description: There should be a free interplay between school and out-of-school life; separation (town and gown, academic seclusion, adherence to an idealized past) makes school knowledge inapplicable to life and infertile in character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure curricula connect to community, family, and civic life; look for numerous points of contact between school activities and students' lives outside school to promote transfer and relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure of school worth: extent of social spirit
rubrics_metrics.description: The measure of the worth of administration, curriculum, and methods is the extent to which they are animated by a social spirit; absence of conditions enabling a permeating social spirit is the great enemy of effective moral training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate schools by how far policies, curricula, and pedagogy foster a permeating social spirit (cooperation, shared responsibility), not merely by content coverage or individual student obedience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid narrow moralizing; view education itself as moral life
rubrics_metrics.description: A narrow moralistic view fails to see that aims like discipline, natural development, culture, social efficiency are themselves moral; 'education is such a life' and maintaining capacity for such education is the essence of morals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject curricula that reduce morals to catechetical instruction or a list of acts; instead cultivate educational forms that embody the social and developmental aims of moral life.
